subject: MAP: performance validation & mutual action plan (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: performance validation and close timeline

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As discussed, Acme Health needs a concrete performance validation in our MAP before we can move to procurement. Key asks from our side:
- Verify latency at our 95th percentile for 1k token responses (target p95 <= 450ms)
- Confirm throughput for steady-state inference of ~10 concurrent sessions (we expect at least 300 TPS aggregate)
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token) under cold-start and warm cache scenarios (goal p95 <= 400ms)
- Provide detailed concurrency envelopes (8 / 12 / 16 sessions) and impact on tail latency

We have attached our workload CSV (Acme_Workload_Spec_v3.csv) with sample request mix and token distributions. Can you propose a short MAP timeline (tasks, owners, dates) so we can aim to close by end of the month? Procurement (Elena Ruiz) will need the results to finalize terms.

Also, we will need a statement about the test environment (shared vs dedicated capacity) and any caveats about caching/quantization used during tests.

Thanks,
Mike

--
Mike Turner
Director, Product Integrations
Acme Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@procureit.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance validation and close timeline

Mike — thanks for the clear asks and the workload file. Draft MAP / bench plan attached (redwood-map-bench-plan.xlsx). High-level proposal below so we can align on scope quickly:

MAP bench plan (summary)
- Workload definition: use Acme_Workload_Spec_v3.csv as primary; supplement with 10% exploratory long-form samples to stress larger responses.
- Metrics: latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), throughput (TPS @ target concurrency), TTFT (p50/p95 cold/warm), CPU/GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit rates.
- Concurrency envelope: run experiments at 4, 8, 12, 16 concurrent sessions (single model variant).
- Environments: run on Dedicated capacity replica (to match expected production) + one run on Hosted to note differences.
- Success criteria (pass): p95 latency <= 450ms AND TTFT p95 <= 400ms AND sustained throughput >= 300 TPS at concurrency=10 with error rate <= 0.5% over 10-minute windows.
- Owners: Redwood (Sooj/Marissa) will run tests and deliver results; Acme (Mike/Eng) to provide test keys, workload confirmations, and access window. Procurement (Elena) to accept final perf report for SOW.
- Timeline (proposed):
  * Aug 22 — confirm workload & test keys (Acme)
  * Aug 23–25 — Redwood runs full bench suite (warm/cold + concurrency sweeps)
  * Aug 27 — deliver preliminary results and short readout
  * Aug 29 — final MAP sign-off and procurement handoff

Questions for you:
1) Can you confirm whether the test data must be redacted / PHI-free? If PHI is required, we will need a Private deployment window.
2) Do you prefer the report as a single PDF and CSV of raw samples?

Attachments: redwood-map-bench-plan.xlsx (test scripts, exact matrix), request for test API key.

If that looks good I’ll kick off the runs on Monday morning.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — plan looks good. A couple clarifications:
- Test data: PHI must be redacted for the first pass; we will provide a synthetic redacted sample for the runs. If you need PHI-level validation later, we will open a Private deployment window but that will push timelines.
- Report format: PDF summary + CSV of raw latency traces is perfect.

We confirmed procurement is on standby — Elena is copied. I also dropped the HubSpot record here: https://hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345 and a DocuSign link for the SOW: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/ACME-SOW-2026.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mike Turner <mike.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@procureit.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance validation and close timeline — preliminary results

Team — ran the full bench matrix this morning on a Dedicated capacity replica (configuration: 4xA100-equivalent, quantized FP16, batch size auto). Summary below; full CSV attached (acme-perf-results-0825.csv) and a short PDF brief (acme-map-performance-report-v1.pdf) will follow.

Key results (warm cache)
- p50 latency: 120 ms
- p95 latency: 410 ms
- p99 latency: 580 ms
- TTFT p50: 95 ms; TTFT p95: 390 ms
- Sustained throughput (measured at concurrency=12): 420 TPS (error rate 0.12%)
- GPU utilization: 72% avg during steady-state windows

Concurrency sweep notes
- 4 sessions: p95 latency 240 ms
- 8 sessions: p95 latency 320 ms
- 12 sessions: p95 latency 410 ms (see above)
- 16 sessions: p95 latency 610 ms — above our agreed SLO but useful to show envelope

Pass/fail against MAP success criteria:
- p95 latency <= 450 ms — PASS
- TTFT p95 <= 400 ms — PASS (390 ms)
- Sustained throughput >= 300 TPS at concurrency=10 — PASS (420 TPS at 12)
- Error rate <= 0.5% — PASS

Caveats and next steps:
- These were run on Dedicated capacity with caching enabled; Hosted runs show +10–20% tail latency.
- We recommend a final run with Acme’s production traffic mix (if you can provide a 10-minute sample) to validate distribution sensitivity.
- If Acme wants improved p99 behavior at 16 concurrent sessions we can explore batching tweaks and KV cache priming.

Attaching results and a short readout. If this aligns with expectations we can confirm the MAP sign-off and loop in procurement for the SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Performance Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance validation and close timeline — final sign-off

Mike / Elena — great to see the results. Based on Marissa’s runs we meet the MAP success criteria as written. Proposed close steps:
- Aug 30: Redwood to deliver final PDF + raw CSV bundle (we'll include run logs and config lines) — Marissa
- Aug 31: Procurement to accept perf report and attach to SOW (Elena)
- Sep 02: Order placement and dedicated capacity start date to be negotiated

Two quick notes:
1) If Acme wants the p99 at 16 concurrent sessions tightened we can target a short optimization sprint (1–2 days) that will likely be included as a minor config change in the SOW.
2) If you need PHI validation we recommend scheduling a Private deployment window; that will add about 10 business days to the timeline.

If you’re comfortable, reply-all with a one-line acceptance and we’ll mark the MAP closed and hand it over to purchases.

Thanks for the fast coordination — excited to move forward.

Best,
Soojin
